assessments.reasoning: Authenticity. The Oracle documentation HTTPS host served the original PeopleBooks PDF. Its cover, copyright page and PDF title identify the October 2022 PeopleTools 8.60 SQR Language Reference for PeopleSoft. The pinned SCES authority table admits official documentation for what its publisher documents at the identified edition. Integrity. I downloaded the exact publisher URL into independent scratch and computed SHA-256 283fce6339ea5eb7cb2a972e5d381ae030271b6f6c536419e459dc605f8fd329 over the original 1,961,126 bytes and reopened those bytes in a separate inspection. Relevance. Chapter 2 BEGIN-PROCEDURE, one-indexed physical and printed pages 60–61, directly addresses the header forms, procedure-local scope and the immediate post-marker underscore. Page 60 contains the syntax, default behavior and locality explanation. Page 61 contains the prefix rule and reserved-variable note. Page 62 confirms both the caller-return colon and the global reference example. Interpretation. The alternative header forms independently establish locality. Ordinary same-name declarations remain procedure-scoped. The described global spelling applies after $, # or & where the applicable form allows the operation. Separate query bindings and persistent storage do not alter the stated name scope. Applicability. The adopter's language-design predicate admits documented claims and requires an edition dimension. The claim has it, shares all authority, edition and revision values with the source, and identifies the active SQR for PeopleSoft language entity. The documented category, descriptive modality and official-documentation role match the adopter and pinned SCES. Contradiction. The same manual's DECLARE-VARIABLE section on pp. 114–115 and errors 007209 and 007211 on pp. 435 and 537 qualify explicit typed declarations. These passages reject an interpretation that the spelling authorizes every variable form or makes a global variable legal in an explicit local typed declaration. Revision 2 attributes the spelling itself to the BEGIN-PROCEDURE description and expressly retains the applicability rules for each marker. The edition-matched developer guide also describes a same-name unprefixed local and the explicit global reference prefix.

challenge.method: Read the complete BEGIN-PROCEDURE section in the exact PDF on physical and printed pp. 60–62 and inspected rendered pages and footer numbering. Checked the same document on pp. 28–29, 63–64, 114–115, 435 and 537 for counterexamples. Searched Oracle's PeopleTools 8.60 materials for contrary or narrower scope, including arguments without LOCAL, LOCAL without arguments, same-name fallback, reserved globals, recursion, returned arguments, ampersand columns, explicit variable declarations and diagnostics 007209 and 007211. Compared the October 2022 Oracle developer guide's Using Local Variables, Passing Arguments and Avoiding Common Programming Errors sections as adverse context from the same publisher.
challenge.results: The default global procedure requires neither localizing header form. LOCAL after the name and declaration with arguments each localize a procedure. The absence of the underscore can select a separate local instead of causing a syntax error. Print-it demonstrates an underscored $ global beside ordinary local arguments. The reserved-variable note confirms underscore-qualified reserved references, and the colon example uses an argument returned to the caller. Persistence across calls and query-column scope are distinct. Ampersand covers database columns or expressions, and the reference separately lists other marker families. Error 007211 gives adverse evidence against a universal permission to declare globals inside a procedure. Error 007209 and DECLARE-VARIABLE constrain the types that typed declarations accept. These limits are consistent with the exact claim about the spelling Oracle describes for applicable declarations and references. The same-edition developer guide also documents the global reference form. No unresolved contrary evidence was found for the scoped documentation claim.

limitations: Independently reviewed as a descriptive report of Oracle's October 2022 PeopleTools 8.60 documentation. No PeopleTools SQR runtime execution, other version coverage or independent source corroboration was used.

The cited global spelling is subject to the underlying command and variable-family rules. In particular, the reference catalogs errors 007209 and 007211 for prohibited typed declaration forms. The revision does not promise that adding an underscore permits a global DECLARE-VARIABLE statement inside a procedure.

Chapter 1 distinguishes & database-column/expression names, $ text/date names, # numeric names, % list names and @ marker-location names. This result is limited to the three markers named in the cited global spelling rule. Argument return, query-column binding and variable retention are separate behaviors.
